# Taxonomy and decision space

**Problem → Decision → Alternatives → Trade-offs → Evaluation → Research.**
These fourteen domains are knowledge responsibilities, not fourteen mandatory pipeline stages. Domains 01–09 describe core ER decisions; 10–12 own research/evaluation; 13–14 own system-level constraints. Scoring and clustering are not interchangeable terms. Related-to edges do not establish same-as membership.

| Domain | Responsibility | Main question |
|---|---|---|
| [01](domains/01-problem-identity.md) | Problem Formulation & Identity Semantics | What does one entity mean, and what output constitutes a correct resolution? |
| [02](domains/02-architecture-orchestration.md) | Pipeline Architecture & Orchestration | How should components interact, route work and revise decisions? |
| [03](domains/03-data-integration.md) | Data Understanding & Integration | Which observations are semantically comparable and sufficiently reliable to use? |
| [04](domains/04-normalization-enrichment.md) | Normalization & Enrichment | Which transformations make values comparable without erasing identity evidence? |
| [05](domains/05-candidate-retrieval.md) | Candidate Generation & Retrieval | Which pairs merit scoring under a candidate budget, and which true matches could be missed? |
| [06](domains/06-comparison-evidence.md) | Comparison Features & Evidence Engineering | What similarities, contradictions and contextual observations should a scorer see? |
| [07](domains/07-matching-scoring.md) | Matching & Scoring | How should evidence be aggregated into a score whose interpretation is clear? |
| [08](domains/08-decision-resolution.md) | Decision Policies & Entity Resolution | When should a score trigger a link, abstention, assignment or entity-membership change? |
| [09](domains/09-master-maintenance.md) | Master Entity Construction & Maintenance | How should resolved entities be represented, updated and corrected without hiding evidence? |
| [10](domains/10-ground-truth.md) | Ground Truth & Labeling | What labeled evidence supports training, evaluation and diagnosis for the actual target population? |
| [11](domains/11-evaluation-diagnostics.md) | Evaluation & Diagnostics | Which measurements reveal local quality, final identity quality and the cost of errors? |
| [12](domains/12-experimentation.md) | Experimentation & Research Methods | Which controlled test would distinguish mechanisms and reduce decision uncertainty? |
| [13](domains/13-scalability-execution.md) | Scalability & Execution | How can a logically valid ER design fit resource and update constraints without concealing quality loss? |
| [14](domains/14-governance-monitoring.md) | Explainability, Governance & Monitoring | How can users understand, audit, correct and monitor identity decisions safely? |

## Boundaries that prevent duplicate knowledge
- Source profiling: **03**; quality-aware evidence: **06**; learned weighting: **07**.
- Single-record transformations: **04**; pair comparisons: **06**.
- Retrieval logic: **05**; physical execution/index maintenance: **13**.
- Score interpretation/calibration: **07**; score-dependent actions and membership: **08**; consumer entity construction: **09**.
- Label construction: **10**; measurements: **11**; experiment procedures: **12**.
- Lifecycle/topology: **02** with resource details in **13** and identity-state consequences in **09**.

## Cross-cutting dependencies
Normalization changes retrieval keys and evidence. Retrieval changes the score/calibration population. Scoring quality does not guarantee entity-quality improvement. Membership decisions affect master attributes and future graph features, which can feed errors back into matching. Privacy constraints can remove otherwise available evidence. Labeling, monitoring and experiments must evaluate these interactions rather than attributing all errors to a matcher.

See [independent architecture dimensions](architecture-dimensions.md), [conceptual contracts](module-contracts.md), [catalog](../CATALOG.md), and [reconciliation](../guides/design-reconciliation.md). Pilot method coverage is deliberately narrower than this taxonomy; the [expansion plan](../guides/expansion-plan.md) records the gap.

# 01 — Problem Formulation & Identity Semantics

**Design question:** What does one entity mean, and what output constitutes a correct resolution?

## Decisions and coverage
- Deduplication within a source; cross-source linkage; multi-source identity resolution. Define the eligible record-pair universe, not just the observed candidate pool.
- Entity types and identity semantics: a person is not a household; an organization may be a legal entity, branch, or operating group. Same-as identity and related-to relationships require different labels.
- One-to-one, one-to-many, and many-to-many constraints depend on whether source rows are unique entities or repeated observations. Temporal identity specifies how name changes, identifier reuse and organizational succession are treated.
- Pairwise links, entity memberships and uncertain identity alternatives are distinct outputs. Specify asymmetric false-merge/missed-match costs and the unit of harm.

## Solution families and useful baselines
- Strict identity with validated identifiers; source-scoped identities; time-indexed identity definitions.
- Independent scored links; constrained assignment with an unmatched option; membership partitions; uncertainty-preserving links.

## Ownership and limitations
Incremental is a lifecycle choice, collective is an inference strategy, and neither changes the meaning of identity by itself.

This is a domain map, not complete L2 method coverage. Unexpanded families are retained for [expansion review](../../guides/expansion-plan.md); mature names are not automatic recommendations.

# 05 — Candidate Generation & Retrieval

**Design question:** Which pairs merit scoring under a candidate budget, and which true matches could be missed?

## Decisions and coverage
- Exact, composite and hierarchical blocking; sorted neighborhood with fixed/adaptive windows.
- Approximate q-gram, inverted-index and canopy methods; locality-sensitive hashing; embedding-based ANN; learned keys and retrieval. These families overlap and are not mandatory separate stages.
- Multi-pass union and adaptive blocking/budgets balance unique true-match coverage against duplicate work, candidate explosion and skew.
- Blocking restricts pair space; similarity filtering uses a specified comparison function and threshold, with exact pruning guarantees only under valid bounds. Retrieval similarity is not identity truth.

## Solution families and useful baselines
- Single exact/composite key as an interpretable baseline; complementary passes with recorded pass provenance.
- Sorted or approximate retrieval when key corruption dominates; vector/learned retrieval when representation, labels and cost justify it.

## Ownership and limitations
Logical retrieval lives here; its indexes, partitioning and distributed execution are owned by 13. Candidate recall must be tested independently of scorer recall.

# 06 — Comparison Features & Evidence Engineering

**Design question:** What similarities, contradictions and contextual observations should a scorer see?

## Decisions and coverage
- String similarities, phonetic/linguistic comparisons and attribute-specific name/address/date/phone features express different error tolerances. Identifier evidence distinguishes exact/partial agreement, namespace compatibility and trusted contradiction.
- Rarity/frequency-aware evidence, source-aware quality features and temporal compatibility change the interpretation of equal similarities.
- Missingness states distinguish both missing, one-sided missing, invalid values and reliable disagreement. Multi-valued aliases/histories require an aggregation policy and count/quality context.
- Embeddings and relationship/graph context may add information but can encode related-to rather than same-as. Feature interactions, provenance groups and dependency checks prevent double counting and label leakage.

## Solution families and useful baselines
- Explicit evidence-state comparison vectors with validity masks.
- Continuous/categorical similarities; grouped multi-representation features; frequency, source, temporal and relational context.

## Ownership and limitations
Comparison computes evidence; 07 estimates its contribution. Graph features derived from predicted memberships require train/test separation and explicit feedback assumptions.

# 04 — Normalization & Enrichment

**Design question:** Which transformations make values comparable without erasing identity evidence?

## Decisions and coverage
- Lexical/Unicode normalization, case and punctuation handling need attribute-specific safety conditions; never assume all identifiers are case-insensitive.
- Structural parsing for names and addresses; linguistic/phonetic transformations, transliteration and language-aware variants.
- Address, phone, date and identifier standardization requires locale, namespace, country and validity context. Alias/variant generation and multiple representations retain ambiguity.
- External enrichment adds coverage and provenance/privacy/dependency risks. Learned parsing, normalization uncertainty and joint normalization/matching remain context-dependent design alternatives.

## Solution families and useful baselines
- Raw plus normalized plus parsed representations; conservative deterministic standardization.
- Language-aware variants; phonetic encodings; external reference enrichment; learned or probabilistic transformations.

## Ownership and limitations
Transforming a single attribute belongs here; comparing two transformed records belongs in 06. Preserve raw values and transformation lineage.

# Define identity before choosing resolution

## Decision question

What does “the same entity” mean for this task, and which assertions may the system publish? Choose a semantic target before similarity, thresholds or graph closure. This card's definitions, examples and recommendations are **Atlas synthesis**, not universal laws for people, organizations or identifiers.

## Problem context

A record is a source observation or administrative representation, not the real-world entity itself. Several rows may describe one person; one household row may describe several people. A row containing payer and beneficiary cannot acquire one person identity without first separating roles. Schema alignment, identifying objects and fusing their attributes are distinct responsibilities in the data-fusion literature.[13]

Specify type and granularity: person versus household, legal organization versus operating brand, building versus dwelling, product model versus physical item. Compare records only for a declared role and type. Cross-type relations such as person-employed-by-organization may be useful without being same-as assertions.

## Relevant assumptions

Strict same-as, within a fixed target definition, is an equivalence relation: reflexive, symmetric and transitive. Fallible predicted links are not guaranteed to satisfy its truth conditions. Related-to predicates need their own direction and algebra; do not borrow transitivity from identity.

**Illustrative counterexample:** Alice and Bob share telephone T1; Bob and Carol share T2; Alice and Carol share neither. “Shares at least one telephone” holds for the first two pairs but not the third. Connected-component closure would assert the missing relationship and could incorrectly merge three distinct people. Shared contact is evidence or a typed relationship, not an identity definition.

An identifier needs issuer, namespace, type, validity interval and reuse policy. Equal local customer numbers in different systems are not global identity. A recycled identifier may denote different entities at different times. Unknown reuse is uncertainty, not permission to assume permanence.

## Available solution families

- **Enduring real-entity identity:** preserve continuity across attribute changes, with [time-scoped evidence](../solutions/identity-semantics/temporal-identity.md). It supports longitudinal histories but needs adjudicated continuity rules.
- **Snapshot/state identity:** identify entity-at-time or episode, explicitly linking states if needed. It suits state reconciliation but deliberately fragments enduring entities.
- **Source-scoped identity:** reconcile administrative accounts inside a namespace without claiming worldwide real-entity equivalence. Cross-source correspondences remain separate assertions.
- **Relationship-only linkage:** publish typed related-to edges or ranked alternatives without collapsing nodes. It preserves legitimate many-to-many associations at the cost of leaving deduplication unresolved.

These targets are competing task definitions, not interchangeable algorithms evaluated against one unlabeled notion of truth.

## Criteria for choosing

Ask which object a downstream action affects, whether past and present records must join, what false equivalence would harm, and which distinctions consumers must retain. Migration, renaming or changing contact information does not decide continuity by itself. Organizational succession may mean continuing operations but a different legal entity; obtain project-specific rules or retain an unresolved succession relationship.

## Trade-off comparison

Enduring identity enables longitudinal aggregation but can hide identifier reuse or succession boundaries. State identity makes time boundaries explicit but can underjoin a person history. Namespace identity avoids unsupported global claims but cannot directly answer global deduplication. Relationship graphs express richer associations but do not provide a partition for counting unique entities. Evaluate each against its declared purpose, not against another target's labels.

## Good baseline candidates

Start with typed, source-scoped observations and conservative identity assertions backed by audited identifier semantics; retain unknown cases. If the question is only current-state reconciliation, use a declared snapshot baseline rather than silently assuming lifetime continuity. Compare with enduring identity only after defining compatible longitudinal truth.

## Prerequisites

Domain-owner definitions, source-row multiplicity, eligible populations and adjudication examples are prerequisites. Optional timestamps help only when their meaning is known. Label guides must distinguish same-as, related-to, different and unknown, including the target role/time; unresolved evidence is not a negative label.

The [resolution decision](resolution-strategy.md) consumes this contract. One-to-one across two files is justified only if each has at most one eligible representation per target unit in scope. Repeated visits or accounts may require many-to-one membership instead. Pair links, assignments, partitions and uncertain alternatives are different output promises. Closure is conditionally excluded for a nontransitive relationship target; probabilistic scoring itself is not excluded.

## Open questions

Can a source key be reassigned? Does account migration preserve person identity, account identity, both or neither? Is a corporate successor the same object at the chosen granularity? Who can authorize changing a definition and relabeling history?

## Related evaluations

[Final output evaluation](../evaluation/entity-resolution-quality.md) must match the promised semantics and include ambiguity, source multiplicity and temporal boundary cases. Compare semantic-policy disagreements separately from retrieval/scorer errors. No Atlas performance result is asserted.

## Links to Solution Cards

[Temporal identity](../solutions/identity-semantics/temporal-identity.md) operationalizes enduring identity; [provenance-preserving survivorship](../solutions/master-records/provenance-survivorship.md) constructs values only after membership. [Master representation](master-representation.md) keeps persistent IDs independent of whichever attribute is displayed.

# 07 — Matching & Scoring

**Design question:** How should evidence be aggregated into a score whose interpretation is clear?

## Decisions and coverage
- Hard deterministic rules; expert-weighted soft rules; additive evidence scoring. A score ranking is not automatically a posterior probability.
- Fellegi–Sunter and likelihood ratios give a statistical interpretation to comparison-state weights; conditional independence supports an additive simplification, not every LR model.
- Supervised logistic regression, GAMs, monotonic/constrained models, gradient boosting and neural record matching offer different feature interactions, interpretability and label/compute demands.
- Rule/ML hybrids, ensembles, weak/semi-supervised methods and source-dependent models need label-bias, transfer and calibration diagnostics.

## Solution families and useful baselines
- Manually assigned contributions → estimated likelihood weights or supervised coefficients, preserving interpretable features. This is a comparison space, not a mandatory upgrade ladder.
- Additive/GAM models with selected interactions; flexible models as controlled challengers when labels and error analysis justify them.

## Ownership and limitations
Learn weights here; 06 owns evidence definitions and 08 owns actions. Candidate selection and label sampling change the population for probability interpretation.
